cards.title: Wendell Berry and the Promise of the Deep Life
cards.blurb: Newport argues that a meaningful life is built on sustained attention to the things that matter - and that cultivating depth is the antidote to a scattered, feed-driven day.

cards.title: On Digital Minimalism
cards.blurb: A short reflection on why decluttering your digital life for thirty days can reset your relationship with technology, and what is worth keeping afterward.

cards.title: The Psychology Behind Why We Can't Stop Messaging
cards.blurb: The hook model in plain language: how triggers, actions, and variable rewards keep us checking in - and why knowing the loop is the first step out of it.

cards.title: How To Start New Habits That Actually Stick
cards.blurb: Three practical steps for making new habits automatic, starting with the two-minute rule. Useful if you want 'less scrolling' to actually stick.

cards.title: Mental Models: The Best Way to Make Intelligent Decisions
cards.blurb: A readable map of the core thinking tools - from inversion to second-order consequences - that help you make better decisions with less noise.

cards.title: Prepare your 'no' and keep it handy
cards.blurb: A two-minute read on deciding in advance what you will decline, so the next tempting ask - or notification - does not get your yes by default.

cards.title: The AI Revolution: The Road to Superintelligence
cards.blurb: A famously thorough two-part explainer of what AI is, where it came from, and why the road ahead is both exciting and hard to predict.

cards.title: The Gentle Singularity
cards.blurb: Altman's short reflection on what it feels like to live through the AI transition - gradual, uneven, and already underway.

cards.title: Machine intelligence, part 1
cards.blurb: An early, readable take on how machine intelligence might scale, and what that could mean for work, science, and everyday life.

cards.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
cards.blurb: A skeptic's view of runaway-AI narratives: Newport argues the more concrete story is how we use these tools right now, for better and worse.

cards.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
cards.blurb: Build neural networks from scratch, line by line, with one of the field's best teachers. For when you would rather understand AI than read about it.

cards.title: How to Do Great Work
cards.blurb: Graham's essay on curiosity, taste, and the compounding effect of working on things you genuinely care about.

cards.title: Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World
cards.blurb: Newport's case that sustained concentration is becoming both rarer and more valuable - and how to train it like a skill.

cards.title: Deep Work and the Good Life
cards.blurb: Why depth is not just a productivity trick but a lifestyle: a craftsman's approach to everything you do, including your attention.

cards.title: How to Focus
cards.blurb: Practical, evidence-informed steps for protecting your attention in an environment engineered to fragment it.

cards.title: How to Stop Procrastinating
cards.blurb: A research-backed look at why we delay - and the small starting rituals that make beginning easier than avoiding.

cards.title: Writing one sentence per line
cards.blurb: Sivers's simple writing practice that forces clarity of thought - one idea, one line, no hiding inside paragraphs.

cards.title: Lazy
cards.blurb: Graham on the difference between laziness and indirection - why ambitious people look lazy while they work on what actually matters.

cards.title: How Can Infinity Come in Many Sizes?
cards.blurb: A mathematician-friendly tour of different infinities - countable, uncountable, and why some are bigger than others.

cards.title: Where Does the Quantum World End and Ours Begin?
cards.blurb: Physicists keep pushing the boundary where quantum strangeness gives way to classical everyday objects - and the line keeps moving.

cards.title: Entanglement Builds Space-Time, Now Magic Gives It Gravity
cards.blurb: How quantum entanglement may literally weave the fabric of space and time - one of the boldest ideas in modern physics, told accessibly.

cards.title: Biology Might Not Be Quantum, but Its Math Is Quantumlike
cards.blurb: The surprising mathematics life shares with quantum theory - a fresh lens on how organisms process information.

cards.title: Ctenophores Aren't Just Beautiful - They're Biological Wonders
cards.blurb: Meet the comb jellies: translucent ocean drifters so evolutionarily strange they may rewrite the animal family tree.

cards.title: One Lab's Quest to Build Space-Time Out of Quantum Particles
cards.blurb: Inside the experiments trying to show in a laboratory that space and time emerge from quantum entanglement.

cards.title: Attention
cards.blurb: What philosophers have meant by attention from William James to today - and why it sits at the heart of perception, agency, and ethics.

cards.title: Well-Being
cards.blurb: What makes a life go well for the one living it? A careful map of hedonism, desire theories, and objective-list views.

cards.title: The Meaning of Life
cards.blurb: Supernatural, naturalist, and nihilist answers to the oldest question - surveyed with unusual clarity and no preaching.

cards.title: Virtue Ethics
cards.blurb: The tradition that asks not 'what should I do?' but 'what kind of person should I be?' - from Aristotle to modern revivals.

cards.title: Philosophy of Technology
cards.blurb: How thinkers have understood our relationship with tools and machines - essential background for anyone questioning their phone habits.

cards.title: Socrates and the Search for Wisdom
cards.blurb: What made Socrates the wisest man in Athens, according to the oracle: knowing how much he did not know.

cards.title: What Doesn't Seem Like Work?
cards.blurb: Graham's compass for finding real interests: the work that feels like play to you but looks hard to everyone else.

cards.title: The Lesson to Unlearn
cards.blurb: School teaches you to optimize for tests; Graham argues the most valuable thing to unlearn is working for the grade instead of the understanding.

cards.title: Cities and Ambition
cards.blurb: Every city whispers a different message about what matters - a vivid frame for choosing where and how to build your life.

cards.title: How to Do What You Love and Make Good Money
cards.blurb: Sivers's compact playbook: the intersection of what you love, what you're good at, and what people pay for - with honest examples.

cards.title: You have enough.
cards.blurb: A short meditation on wanting less, from someone who ran a company, sold it, and gave the money away.

cards.title: The Beginner's Guide to Deliberate Practice
cards.blurb: Why 10,000 hours of casual experience isn't mastery, and what deliberate, feedback-driven practice looks like instead.
